plan: With a private value of $24, I want to maximize potential profit. Since the winner pays the third-highest bid, I'll aim to bid strategically. Given the $0-$49 range, most rational bidders will bid near their private value. I'll bid slightly above my value at $26 to increase winning chances. This allows some buffer if others bid similarly. If others bid much higher/lower, I might adjust, but without previous round history, a modest premium seems prudent.

My value is $16. In a first-round game with no prior history, a good strategy is to bid slightly above my value but not too aggressively. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0-$49, other bidders might have values higher or lower. I'll aim to bid around my value plus a modest premium to increase my chances of winning while minimizing overpayment. A bid around $20 seems reasonable - high enough to compete but not so high that I risk significant loss.

With a private value of $24, I want to bid strategically. Since the prize is awarded to the highest bidder at the third-highest price, I'll aim to bid slightly above my true value but not excessively. My goal is to win if my bid is competitive. I'll bid around $25-26 to give myself a buffer above my true value while not overpaying. This allows potential profit if I win and minimizes loss if I overbid.
